aarti.tek: Om, victory to Śiva, who is the sacred syllable Om; victory, O Lord, to Śiva who is Om! You are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva, and you bear your consort as half of your body.
aarti.pad1: You shine with one face (as Viṣṇu), four faces (as Brahmā) and five faces (as Śiva), adorned with the swan seat, the Garuḍa seat and the bull for a mount. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: With two arms, four graceful arms and ten arms you look most beautiful; beholding your three forms, the people of the three worlds are enchanted. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: You wear the rosary of beads, the garland of forest flowers and the garland of skulls; sandal paste and musk adorn you, and you bear the moon on your forehead. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: White robes, yellow silk and a tiger skin are on your limbs; Brahmā and the gods, Sanaka and the sages, and the bhūtas are your companions. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: In your hands you hold the water pot, the discus and the trident; you are the maker of the world, its destroyer and its sustainer. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: The undiscerning see Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva as separate; within the syllable Om the three are one. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: Whoever sings this āratī of the Lord of the three guṇas gains the fruit the heart desires, says Śivānanda Svāmī. ॥7॥
aarti.tek2: Victory to Śiva, who is Om; O Hara, victory to Śiva who is Om! You are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva, bearing your consort as half of your body.
